in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a few key questions.

**First, how many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. Just the one child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances better.

**Are you currently responsible for Alex, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am responsible for Alex, but no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Can you tell me where Alex is currently living, and why Alex isn't living with you at the moment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent - my ex-partner. We separated a while back, and Alex stayed living with them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you explaining that situation. That's quite common after a separation.

**Are you still involved in supporting Alex financially, or do you contribute towards Alex's living costs or upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I still contribute towards Alex's needs - things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you for providing that detail.

**What is your current residency status? Are you a UK resident, and if so, for how long have you been residing in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK resident. I live in Manchester - been here my whole life actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's useful context.

**What is your current nationality or immigration status? Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status or another form of visa?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**One more question to complete the picture: Is Alex a British citizen, or does Alex have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now carefully review your situation against the Child Benefit eligibility rules.

Based on what you've told me:
- You are responsible for Alex
- Alex does not live with you (Alex lives with their other parent)
- You do contribute financially to Alex's needs
- You are a British citizen and UK resident
- Alex is a British citizen

The key issue here relates to whether you meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit. Child Benefit is payable to the person who is "responsible" for a child, but there are specific rules about what "responsible" means and how it interacts with living arrangements.

**Before I make my final assessment, I need one clarification: Are you currently receiving any other benefits (such as Universal Credit, Tax Credits, or any other means-tested benefits), and are you the main carer or primary household earner for Alex in any formal sense?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any other benefits. And no, I'm not the main carer - Alex lives with their other parent full-time, so they're the main carer really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to make a decision.

Based on your circumstances, I need to inform you that you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit is paid to the person who is **wholly or mainly responsible** for a child. In your situation, while you do contribute financially to Alex's needs, Alex lives full-time with their other parent, who is the main carer and the person who is wholly or mainly responsible for Alex's day-to-day upbringing and care.

The fact that you make financial contributions doesn't establish you as the person who is wholly or mainly responsible for Alex. That status belongs to the parent with whom Alex lives and who provides the primary care.

Your ex-partner, as the person with whom Alex lives and who is the main carer, would be the eligible person to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope this clarifies your situation. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or other support you might be entitled to, please feel free to ask.
